```sql
-- name: top_customers
-- owner: sales
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
WITH tenant_customers AS (
    SELECT c.id,
           c.email,
           c.company,
           c.country_code
      FROM customers c
     WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
),
order_agg AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)           AS order_count,
           max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT tc.id,
       tc.email,
       tc.company,
       tc.country_code,
       oa.revenue,
       oa.order_count,
       oa.last_order_at
  FROM tenant_customers tc
  JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.customer_id = tc.id
 WHERE oa.last_order_at >= %(from)s
   AND oa.last_order_at <  %(to)s
 ORDER BY oa.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

Het origineel koppelde alle klanten van alle tenants aan de orderaggregaten via een nested loop die de hash-aggregate ~9800 keer herhaalde. Deze versie groepeert de orders één keer per klant, beperkt de klanten eerst tot de tenant en verbindt die met een hash join. Resultaat, kolommen en ORDER BY blijven gelijk, omdat `max(created_at)` gelijk is aan de DISTINCT ON-uitkomst.
